q: The Picard–Lindelöf theorem guarantees a unique local solution to ẋ = f(x,t), x(0)=x₀ when f is:
opts: Continuous in t and Lipschitz in x (locally)
exp: Picard–Lindelöf requires local Lipschitz continuity in x (not just continuity). Continuous-only gives existence (Peano) but not uniqueness. The Lipschitz condition controls divergence of nearby solutions.
